questions.q: A Class A GFCI is designed to trip when the ground-fault current reaches approximately:
questions.why: A Class A GFCI opens the circuit on an imbalance of about 4–6 mA between the live and identified conductors, low enough to protect people.

questions.q: On a 120/208 V three-phase wye system, the 208 V is measured:
opts: From any line to any other line
questions.why: Line-to-neutral gives 120 V (one winding); line-to-line gives 120 × √3 = 208 V.

questions.q: If the frequency applied to an inductor doubles, its inductive reactance:
questions.why: XL = 2πfL is directly proportional to frequency: double f, double XL.

The synchronous speed of a 6-pole motor on a 60 Hz supply is:
An induction motor has a synchronous speed of 1 800 r/min and runs at 1 725 r/min. The slip is approximately:
To reverse the rotation of a three-phase induction motor:
questions.why: Swapping any two lines reverses the phase sequence, which reverses the rotating field and the motor.

questions.q: A transformer steps 600 V down to 120 V. Its turns ratio (primary to secondary) is:
questions.why: EP/ES = NP/NS = 600/120 = 5:1. Voltage follows turns.

questions.q: The rated secondary line current of a 75 kVA, three-phase transformer with a 208 V secondary is approximately:
The secondary circuit of a current transformer must never be:
opts: Opened while the primary is energized
questions.why: With the primary energized, an open CT secondary develops a dangerously high voltage. Short the secondary before removing instruments.

questions.q: The system neutral is bonded to ground:
opts: At the transformer and every sub-panel
questions.why: Neutral and bond join once, at the service. Downstream, they remain separated so neutral current never flows on bonding paths.

questions.q: In a sub-panel supplied from the main service, the neutral bar must be:
questions.why: Downstream of the service the neutral is isolated; only the bond bar connects to the enclosure.

questions.q: The maximum standard overcurrent protection for a #10 AWG copper conductor in general branch-circuit use is:
questions.why: The small-conductor limits are #14 → 15 A, #12 → 20 A, #10 → 30 A.

questions.q: The maximum continuous load permitted on a 100 A breaker (not 100%-rated) is:
questions.why: Continuous loads are limited to 80% of the device rating: 0.8 × 100 = 80 A.

questions.q: Motor branch-circuit conductors are generally sized at a minimum of:
opts: 125% of the full-load current from the code tables
questions.why: Conductors are sized at not less than 125% of the table full-load current for the motor's horsepower and voltage.

questions.q: Motor overload protection is sized from:
questions.why: Overloads protect the specific machine, so they are set from the nameplate FLA (with service-factor allowances). Conductors use the table value; overloads use the nameplate.

questions.q: In a motor control circuit, stop buttons and safety interlocks are connected:
questions.why: Any single NC device opening must stop the motor, so stops and interlocks are NC in series; starts are NO in parallel.

questions.q: After a power failure, a motor wired with three-wire control and a seal-in contact will:
opts: Remain stopped until the start button is pressed
questions.why: The seal-in contact drops out with the supply, so the circuit provides low-voltage protection: no automatic restart.

questions.q: A series circuit of three lamps has one burned-out (open) lamp. The voltage measured across the open lamp is:
questions.why: No current flows, so no voltage drops across the good lamps; the entire source voltage appears across the open.

questions.q: Two 100 Ω resistors connected in parallel have a total resistance of:
questions.why: Equal resistors in parallel: RT = R ÷ n = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 Ω.

questions.q: The power dissipated when 12 A flows through a connection with 0.5 Ω of resistance is:
questions.why: P = I²R = 12² × 0.5 = 144 × 0.5 = 72 W — which is why a loose, resistive connection runs hot.

questions.q: A 1 500 W heater operating for 8 hours consumes:
questions.why: W = P × t = 1.5 kW × 8 h = 12 kWh.

questions.q: The general maximum conduit fill for three or more insulated conductors is:
questions.why: With three or more conductors, the combined cross-section may occupy no more than 40% of the raceway area.

Under the CEC, the generally accepted maximum voltage drop for a branch circuit alone, and for the total from supply to load, is:
questions.why: The long-standing limits are 3% for the final branch circuit or feeder and 5% overall from the supply point to the point of utilization.
